intended_object: An auxiliary, certificate-carrying version of the unbounded μ-operator: given a partial predicate p : ℕ →. Bool and a proof that some n has p n = true with all earlier values defined, it returns the least such n together with proofs of its properties (inferred from the docstring and from its use in defining Nat.rfind).
explanation: The body uses well-founded recursion on `lbp p` (well-founded by `wf_lbp p H`), starting at 0. At each m it uses H to show that p m is defined; it moves on to m+1 when p m is false and returns m when p m is true. That is correct. Its only uses in Mathlib are right after its definition (lines 88–94 of Mathlib/Computability/Partrec.lean): it defines the partial function `Nat.rfind`, whose domain is the condition in H and whose value is `(rfindX p h).1`, and it supplies the proofs of `rfind_spec` and `rfind_min`. It is therefore an implementation device bundling the witness with its proofs. The mathematical object, the μ-operator, is `Nat.rfind`. If it were judged as the μ-operator itself, it would be faithful, since ℕ and Bool are the natural setting for minimisation.
